featured_reviews.name: Pranali Karpe
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited a new restaurant in Nalasopara West with my father for an evening snack, eager to try it out. We started off by ordering Sada Rawa Dosa and Onion Rawa Dosa. Unfortunately, the waiter appeared to take our order randomly and brought us Masala Rawa Dosa instead of the Sada. When we pointed out the mistake, he seemed reluctant to acknowledge it and almost began to argue, which we didn’t want to engage in. To avoid further confrontation, my dad suggested we just go ahead and eat what was served.

The most disappointing part was that the owner, who was sitting at the reception, didn’t make an effort to check on us or address the issue. We also ordered tea, but after waiting for over 30 minutes with no sign of it, we asked the waiter about our order. He nonchalantly replied, “Chai bann rahe hai,” which felt unacceptable after such a long wait. When we eventually asked for the bill, the waiter claimed he was still bringing the tea—something we no longer wanted.

While paying the bill, I mentioned our experience to the owner, who simply nodded without addressing our concerns. On a positive note, the quality and quantity of the food were excellent, and the ambiance was nice. However, the service left much to be desired.

Visited Dakshina Katha expecting an authentic South Indian breakfast, but it turned out to be quite disappointing.

We ordered benne masala dosa, Mysore masala dosa, ghee podi thatte idli, and filter coffee. The benne masala dosa was extremely doughy and not crispy at all, more like a kal dosa.
